answers.explanation: Nothing writes to a closed segment, so reading and rewriting it needs no locks.
Only each key's latest value survives.
One key every few kilobytes is enough.
The memtable is also backed by a write-ahead log for crash safety.
Newer data wins, so check newest first.
So lookups for missing keys don't read every segment.
LevelDB and RocksDB level; Cassandra defaults to size-tiered.
